source.title: Alignment-Weighted DPO: A principled reasoning approach to improve safety alignment
source.authors: Meng-Xuan Hu; Vivek Datla; Anoop Kumar; Zi-Han Guan; Sheng Li; Alfy Samuel; Da-Ben Liu

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether attacks bypass safety using its own prefix attack and additional attack evaluations, but does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or per-token KL experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fine-tuning, first-token effects, and neuron pruning; cited results are not recorded as rows. Its own neuron-pruning results concern whether safety depends on reasoning, not whether safety is localized in a small set of parameters. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL or test a compliant opening. Table 10 tests appending <think></think>; Table 13 reports additional attack evaluations.
record.test_reason: This is a defence-method paper (CoT safety SFT plus AW-DPO). It cites shallow alignment [40] as motivation and reports how robust its own method is. Its 'superficial alignment' test is a different construct: whether safety depends on reasoning-critical attention heads. It does not measure token depth, compliant-opening prefill, harmful or benign fine-tuning of safety-trained models, or safety-localized weights. Table 10's appended '<think></think>' only makes its own CoT model skip reasoning; it is not a compliant opening. Table 13's GPTFuzz and PAP are template and persuasion jailbreaks run as a method comparison. No row bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with three qualifications. The authors' 'superficial' means refusals do not depend on reasoning; they did not measure token depth. The prefix-attack robustness claim concerns their AW-DPO model, which by its numbers is Llama-3.2-3B. They also conclude that CoT SFT and AW-DPO lower SorryBench ASR versus SFT, DPO and other baselines while keeping MMLU utility.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses head deactivation, CoT safety fine-tuning, and AW-DPO; it does not apply the original harmful/benign fine-tuning or per-token KL recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested prefix attack changes ASR by benchmark category, with some categories increasing and Encoding & Encryption decreasing. The attack evaluations also differ by attack method (GPTFuzz versus PAP).

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing the top 10% of reasoning-probed heads in layers 1–11 cuts reasoning accuracy by 31–42%. Llama Guard safety rate stays at 97–100% in LLaMA2-7B, LLaMA2-13B and LLaMA3.2-3B. Probing heatmaps for Llama-2-7B-Chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct show the same pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal behaviour in aligned chat models is largely independent of reasoning-critical attention heads, which the authors take as evidence of 'superficial' alignment.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says full code will be released upon acceptance. CoT dataset URL: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/cot_safety_data-3C51/
record.problems: The head-pruning safety evaluation reports no uncertainty estimates; the tested prefix attack concerns one model whose identity is not given in Table 10, and the prefix is not a compliant opening. Table 13 does not specify the attack procedures. The paper reports GPT-4o judge prompt correlations of 0.6658, 0.9116, and 0.5761 for full, response-only, and reasoning-only scores, respectively.
record.rows_left_out: Table 13's LLM Score (Adaptive) values were not recorded because the text does not define the score sufficiently to establish that it measures harmful-completion rate. Utility measures and general safety benchmark comparisons were omitted because they do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning of a safety-trained model.
No benign fine-tuning of a safety-trained model measuring harmful compliance. Table 1's Alpaca SFT is applied to base models without safety training.
No per-token KL or any position-wise analysis.
No prefilled compliant opening, adversarial suffix or decoding attack on any model.
Pruning targets reasoning heads, not safety-critical weights or ranks.
No test of which data or objective causes token-shallow safety.
AW-DPO and CoT SFT are not shown to extend safety beyond the first tokens, and are not tested against prefill or fine-tuning attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Recommend reclassifying from 'tests/T2' to 'uses_without_test/T4' and dropping the reader's V4 labels. Table 10 and Table 13 are robustness checks of the authors' own method using non-V4 attacks. The reader's 'challenges' label also mixed comparator and own-method rows. Side observation, not a version test: Table 11 shows CoT Safety SFT on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct raising Base ASR from 3.41% to 6.14%, though average ASR falls. This is safety data, not benign data, so it is not V2. The SorryBench judge is GPT-4o; its correlations under a perturbed prompt are moderate (0.58–0.91).

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning experiment on a safety-trained chat model; no few-to-hundreds-example sweep or refusal-removal result.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning experiment measuring increased harmful compliance in a safety-trained chat model.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Tests the <think></think> prefix attack and two named attack methods, but not a prefilled compliant opening or decoding changes; Table 13 does not specify the attack procedures.
Does not test whether a small set of safety-specific weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.

Does not identify whether particular training data or objectives caused shallowness. It does test whether safety performance depends on reasoning-critical heads; that result is recorded under fits_no_version.
CoT fine-tuning and AW-DPO are evaluated for safety, but the study does not measure whether they spread safety beyond the first response tokens or test persistence of such depth.

rows.operation_detail: Append “<think></think>” to the end of the prompt as a prefix attack.
rows.measure: Attack success rate (ASR; lower is safer)
rows.note: The rate rises, but remains low; the authors say safety performance is preserved. Table 10 does not name the model.
rows.check: Own-method robustness check. Appending '<think></think>' skips reasoning in the authors' CoT model; it is not a compliant opening or adversarial suffix against refusal. The subject can be identified: Table 10 baseline values (1.14%, 0.27, 0.09, 1.36, 0.73, 0.58; utility 48.52%) match Llama-3.2-3B +AW-DPO in Table 1.

reader_labels.condition: AW-DPO model under the appended <think></think> prefix attack
reader_labels.reason: The prefix produces small increases in some ASR categories but does not produce high harmful-completion rates; rates decrease in Encoding & Encryption (R1–R6).
